title: Innovation assessment
scope: LabourLens helps policy researchers check Singapore labour-market figures against official reports from early 2020 to mid-2026.
abstract: It brings statistics, explanations and source links together so analysts can spend less time searching and more time checking what the evidence means.
approach: The assistant searches official reports, looks up statistics and calculates changes using checked records.
It shows sources alongside answers and asks for clarification or declines when evidence is missing.
Published figures retain their dates, definitions and release versions so unlike measures are not silently combined.
An annual-average calculation requires four complete quarterly rates from the same measure and is not an official annual rate.
Recent changes to calculations, follow-up questions and explanations have not been evaluated.

sections.title: How I would improve it
sections.summary: These are proposals, not built improvements or demonstrated gains.

subsections.title: Finding evidence and answering well
paragraphs: Search found relevant passages more often, but full-answer tests did not demonstrate a reliable improvement.

subsections.title: Keeping evidence current
paragraphs: Saved source versions make updates traceable, but collecting and checking new releases still needs an operator.

proposals.title: Shorter waits
proposals.gap: The evaluated middle answer time was about 14 seconds, and showing progress does not shorten the full wait.
proposals.measure: Try independent work at the same time, reuse permitted previous lookups and shorten unnecessary preparation.
proposals.threshold: Compare typical and slow answers on the same questions, keeping accuracy, safety and cost at least as good.

proposals.title: Retry the question-routing idea
proposals.gap: Two earlier trials sorted questions faster but misdirected legitimate questions and failed safety or reliability checks.
proposals.measure: Test an untried choice between supported and unsupported topics while keeping existing harmful-question handling and the normal research fallback.
proposals.threshold: Set the rules before testing fresh reviewed questions and reject any change that wrongly excludes legitimate research or weakens safety.

proposals.title: Broader, independent evaluation
proposals.gap: Earlier tests cover 2024 to 2026 only, and one human reviewed labels initially drafted by artificial intelligence.
proposals.measure: Ask independent analysts to review unseen questions, including 2020 to 2023, and test each protection separately.
proposals.threshold: Report answer support, calculation errors, disagreement and harmless questions wrongly blocked without adjusting the system to fit the test.

proposals.title: Useful calculations with clear limits
proposals.gap: The new annual-average calculation is unevaluated, and a previous attempt to calculate from report tables failed.
proposals.measure: Check complete inputs and definitions for annual averages, and add calculations only where analysts have a demonstrated need.
proposals.threshold: Compare results with checked examples and refuse missing values or uncertain table layouts rather than guessing.

proposals.title: Careful source updates
proposals.gap: A new release or changed definition can make a previously correct answer misleading.
proposals.measure: Schedule approved source collection, retain earlier releases and check definitions, coverage and reuse rights before publication.
proposals.threshold: Block failed updates, show when evidence is stale and test answers before adding sources or topics.

sections.title: Production deployment and security
sections.summary: The public prototype runs on one server with shared access codes, not a government production service.
paragraphs: Source-rights checks, simulated attack tests and activity records exist today, but shared access, local records and recovery still need stronger controls.

subsections.title: Evidence and review
paragraphs: Sources and activity are visible, but a valid quotation does not prove that it supports the answer.

subsections.title: Security and privacy
paragraphs: Simulated attacks found weaknesses, and neither those tests nor the proposed controls establish safety or legal compliance.

subsections.title: Today and the proposed replacement
paragraphs: Live features are not simulated, but hostile-service tests are artificial and the replacements below are not built.

proposals.title: A dependable service
proposals.gap: One server and local records have not demonstrated reliable service under load or after failure.
proposals.measure: Separate source updates from answers, spread requests across replaceable workers, retain versioned evidence and keep shared limits and activity records.
proposals.threshold: Test heavy demand, interrupted answers, restoration, switching to a spare service and return to the last approved version.

proposals.title: Protect people, data and access
proposals.gap: Shared codes cannot enforce individual permissions, and outside model processing has not been approved for restricted information.
proposals.measure: Add government sign-in, source permissions, secure credentials, attack filtering, usage limits and legal review of provider data use, location and retention.
proposals.threshold: Prove that restricted information stays out of unauthorised answers and records, and obtain security and privacy approval before using it.

proposals.title: Independent security checks
proposals.gap: Documents can contain hostile instructions, and software or outside connections can introduce risks.
proposals.measure: Keep documents as evidence rather than instructions, restrict outside connections, review software suppliers and commission independent security testing.
proposals.threshold: Test hostile passages and harmless look-alikes, repair serious findings and check that activity records reveal unauthorised changes.

proposals.title: Clear operational ownership
proposals.gap: Stored feedback does not yet improve answers, and availability, recovery and spending limits remain unverified.
proposals.measure: Assign support owners, agree service and spending limits, review reported failures and protect backups and retained activity records.
proposals.threshold: Demonstrate alerts, spending stops and recovery, then require approval before moving from a public-data pilot to a more robust trial.

sections.title: Making it ready for government use across departments
sections.summary: Shared use needs accountable decisions and separate access, not just more users.

proposals.title: Governance and human responsibility
proposals.gap: A plausible answer can be wrong, especially when it informs a consequential policy decision.
proposals.measure: Use Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework as a review reference, assess risks and impacts, require human review and record approved uses and changes.
proposals.threshold: Named owners approve each change against evidence and monitor deterioration without treating this proposal as certification or compliance.

proposals.title: Separate departmental evidence
proposals.gap: Departments may hold different permissions, definitions and source licences.
proposals.measure: Keep departmental collections and permissions separate while sharing only approved read-only capabilities and documented source-collection rules.
proposals.threshold: Test that one department cannot see another's restricted evidence and verify ownership, definitions and a source-rights register before onboarding.

proposals.title: Roll out only after evidence
proposals.gap: Each department adds new information, users and risks that the prototype has not tested.
proposals.measure: Start with a public-data pilot, strengthen the service through a controlled trial and admit departments one at a time.
proposals.threshold: Require data-owner approval, staff preparation, support readiness and a way to stop or reverse each stage without promising dates.

limitations: Development questions shaped the design, and reused test questions are not independent proof of better answers.
Answer labels and automatic judging are not independent human ground truth.
Citations and correct arithmetic can still support the wrong interpretation or use the wrong inputs.
Expanded sources, recent changes and proposed production controls have not been fully evaluated.

components.current: Shared codes and one web worker.
components.replacement: Proposed individual government sign-in and permission checks.

components.current: One server with local records and temporary limits.
components.replacement: Proposed shared records, queued work and replaceable workers.

components.current: Local source copies and read-only data access.
components.replacement: Proposed protected versioned storage and isolated data access.

components.current: Outside provider terms and data location are unverified.
components.replacement: Proposed approved providers, secure credentials and enforced processing rules.

components.current: Automated deployment exists, but recovery is unverified.
components.replacement: Proposed release checks, backups and tested restoration.
